items.stem: What is the difference between merge and rebase?

options.text: Merge preserves history with a merge commit; rebase replays commits onto a new base
options.rationale: Correct: that is the core distinction.
Rebase moves commits, it does not delete work.

options.text: Merge can only be done once per repo
They produce identical history in all cases

items.explanation: Correct: that is the core distinction.

items.stem: Which TWO are safe recovery tools after a bad change? (Select TWO.)

options.text: git reflog to find a lost commit
options.rationale: Correct: reflog tracks recent HEAD positions.

options.text: git revert to undo a commit with a new commit
options.rationale: Correct: revert safely undoes without rewriting history.

options.text: Force-pushing over shared history without warning

items.explanation: Correct: reflog tracks recent HEAD positions.

items.stem: Why avoid rebasing branches others have already pulled?

options.text: It rewrites commit history and causes divergence for collaborators
options.rationale: Correct: rewriting shared history creates conflicts for others.
Speed is not the concern here.
Rebasing is allowed; the issue is shared history.
It does not corrupt the repo.

items.explanation: Correct: rewriting shared history creates conflicts for others.
